name: bg-singularity

frames.best_why: Frame 4 shows the brightest blue and orange rim with the clearest gas plume at the top right.

tagline: A black void ringed by a thin blue and orange halo of gas.
summary: A full-bleed shader that renders something like a black hole: a dark circular void edged with a glowing rim that runs cold blue on one side and warm orange on the other, with wispy gas trailing into black.
appearance: Against pure black sits a large dark disc outlined by a thin luminous ring. The lower-left arc is icy blue and the upper-right arc is warm orange, and faint streaked plumes bleed off the ring toward both corners.
behaviour: The ring and its gas drift very slowly, with the plume shape creeping around the rim and the rim fading in and out. There is no input beyond a slow continuous loop.
search_phrases: dark background with a bright rim
use_when: A space or science-fiction page needs an atmospheric glowing singularity behind its copy.
avoid_when: It is a full-frame absolute shader whose motion is slow enough that it can read as a still.
customise: hue, saturation, brightness, speed, mouseSensitivity, damping and an optional noise setting tune the shader; className adds styles.
weight_why: A full-screen fragment shader with a multi-step loop, run every frame.

a11y.note: Decorative shader with no reduced-motion check; the white caption only stays readable over the dark centre.

issues: All six frames differ so little that the moving shader is easy to mistake for a static image.
polish_why: Intricate rim and gas tendrils with real craft; the motion is too slow to register.
title: Singularity Background
